HyznrdDSSGM.summary: Ben Eater's short update announcing his plan to build another 8-bit computer from scratch on camera. It kicks off the breadboard computer series that became widely known.
HyznrdDSSGM.why: HN repeatedly recommends the series it launched as the best way to understand how a CPU works, praised for Eater's clear teaching.

HxaD_trXwRE.summary: Rob Pike shows how the Go text/template lexer is built, using state functions, goroutines and channels. The talk was given at a Google Technology User Group in Sydney in 2011.
HxaD_trXwRE.why: HN returns to it for years as an elegant introduction to writing a lexer that is easy to follow even without a parsing background.

HyzD8pNlpwI.summary: Michael Steil's 33c3 talk explains essentially everything about the Game Boy: CPU, video hardware, peripherals, and the tricks used by games and demos. It revives the era of counting clock cycles around hardware limits.
HyzD8pNlpwI.why: HN treats it as the standard starting point for Game Boy emulator writers and homebrew developers, with several calling it one of their favorite talks.

HaEPXoXVf2k.summary: Rick Houlihan's AWS re:Invent 2018 deep dive on advanced DynamoDB design patterns. It covers index overloading, GSI sharding, composite keys, graph processing and transactions.
HaEPXoXVf2k.why: The go-to recommendation for learning DynamoDB data modeling, with many saying it made access-pattern-driven design click.

HKQDSgBHPfY.summary: John Sotos, a physician and former Intel chief medical officer, argues at DEF CON 25 that genetic diseases are exploitable vulnerabilities in the genome. He warns that CRISPR and related tools will make malicious genome hacks and targeted bioweapons feasible.
HKQDSgBHPfY.why: Recommended whenever DNA testing, CRISPR or bioweapons come up, often as the talk that made commenters decide to keep their DNA out of databases.

HOuZyOKa91o.summary: Ruby developer Avdi Grimm gives a seven-minute tour of Pharo Smalltalk's development environment, focusing on tools like search-by-example and the integrated, live coding experience.
HOuZyOKa91o.why: HN recommends it as a quick, compelling look at what Smalltalk tooling feels like, especially for Ruby programmers.

HCUct4NlxE0.summary: A short street-level clip of Joe Ades, the New York pitchman who sold vegetable peelers to crowds on the sidewalk. It shows his patter, showmanship and crowd handling in action.
HCUct4NlxE0.why: HN treats him as a master class in salesmanship and live presentation, where how you sell matters more than what you sell.

HeQX2HjkcNo.summary: Veritasium's explainer on Godel's incompleteness theorems and the limits of mathematical proof, tracing set theory, Hilbert's program and the road to Turing and modern computing.
HeQX2HjkcNo.why: HN commenters recommend it as a clear, accessible introduction to incompleteness and the self-referential proof idea.

HI09kat_GeI.summary: Sean Carroll introduces his video series on the biggest ideas in physics, such as symmetry, space and matter, as informal discussions with follow-up Q&A videos. This is the short opening video of the series.
HI09kat_GeI.why: HN commenters recommend the series as engaging, substantial physics with just enough math for non-specialists.

HQYsFshbkYw.summary: Bisqwit builds a Doom or Duke Nukem 3D style software-rendered 3D engine in C from scratch, supporting non-Euclidean geometry. It covers vector rotation and portal rendering with sped-up, tool-assisted coding.
HQYsFshbkYw.why: A favorite on Ask HN lists of programming YouTube channels, praised for mind-blowing systems and graphics programming and a watchable coding style.

HUEvRyemKSg.summary: Cory Doctorow's 28c3 keynote argues that the copyright wars were just a skirmish and that the real fight will be a war on the general-purpose computer. He explains why locked-down devices, DRM and surveillance tools all depend on removing general computation.
HUEvRyemKSg.why: HN returns to it constantly as a prescient talk, cited whenever threads cover DRM, locked-down devices, app verification or restrictions on running your own software.

H9B5mYfBPlY.summary: A long Tim Ferriss podcast interview with physician Gabor Mate on trauma, addiction, depression, ADHD and ayahuasca. Mate explains how childhood stress and emotional pain underlie many addictions and illnesses.
H9B5mYfBPlY.why: HN recommends it as a thoughtful, honest look at the causes of addiction and depression, and as a deeper Mate interview than most.

HJ-719EGIts.summary: A 2007 Google Tech Talk in which Cliff Click of Azul Systems presents a lock-free concurrent hash table that scales to 768 CPUs. He explains why it is correct by reasoning in a different way than usual happens-before and memory-order arguments.
HJ-719EGIts.why: HN regards it as one of the best technical talks, a deep and clear walkthrough of scalable lock-free hash tables built on compare-and-swap.

Hhy7JUinlu0.summary: A clip from the 2011 film Margin Call in which senior partners hold an emergency meeting and decide to sell off toxic assets immediately. It is set at the start of the 2008 financial crisis.
Hhy7JUinlu0.why: HN cites the scene as a model of clear, decisive communication and of leaders acting fast to survive, and recommends the film as the best take on 2008.

HLRdruqQfRk.summary: Tom Scott-style absurdist research by tom7 for SIGBOVIK 2021, using machine learning to discover letterforms that are 'uppercaser' than uppercase A and lowercaser than lowercase. It is a comedic, technically inventive deep dive with fonts and a paper.
HLRdruqQfRk.why: Tom7 is an HN favorite, and this video is praised as hilarious, educational silly ML that keeps getting better.

Hqw57GJSrac.summary: Cliff Click, author of HotSpot's JIT compiler, shares hard-won advice for people writing virtual machines at the VMSS16 workshop. Topics include interpreters, JITs and performance lessons.
Hqw57GJSrac.why: HN recommends it, and Cliff Click's talks in general, as practical wisdom from someone who built HotSpot and worked on Azul's VMs.

HB5TrK7A4pI.summary: Gerald Sussman's 2011 Strange Loop keynote argues we still do not know how to compute, comparing biological systems with how we program machines. It touches on propagators, constraint programming and robustness.
HB5TrK7A4pI.why: HN commenters recommend it as a mind-expanding talk on rethinking programming, and cite it in threads on propagators, constraints and brittleness.

HLNhPMQnWu4.summary: A two-minute John Cleese monologue showing the pathology of extremism, explaining why it feels good and how it drives out moderates.
HLNhPMQnWu4.why: Shared in heated-discussion threads as a short, witty take on why extremism is appealing.

HPuvDm8IC-4.summary: Liz Rice builds a container from scratch in about 100 lines of Go, showing that a container is not a lightweight VM but a set of Linux kernel features and flags.
HPuvDm8IC-4.why: HN recommends it as an accessible way to remove the magic from Docker and understand how containers work.

H46ON2FB30U.summary: A four-minute tour of the TeXmacs scientific editor, showing math typing, figures, citations, a drawing tool, document styles, HTML export, presentations and animations.
H46ON2FB30U.why: Recommended as the quickest way to see what TeXmacs can do, as a WYSIWYG alternative to LaTeX.

HdHlfiOAJyE.summary: First session of MIT 15.401 Finance Theory I (Fall 2008) taught by Andrew Lo, giving a course overview and introducing core finance concepts. The course ran during the 2007-08 financial crisis.
HdHlfiOAJyE.why: Recommended as a free, first-principles finance course for software engineers wanting to learn business and finance.

Hvx4xXhZMrU.summary: Making-of video about ROM City Rampage, the NES version of Retro City Rampage, covering how the game's core was crunched to run on real 8-bit hardware and how NES games are made.
Hvx4xXhZMrU.why: Recommended as a fascinating look at fitting a modern game into NES constraints.

Hy4QjmKzF1c.summary: The School of Life sets out principles for making attractive cities, arguing that the art has been lost in the modern world.
Hy4QjmKzF1c.why: Recommended in urban planning and housing threads as a concise summary of what makes cities livable and beautiful.

H6ZFzEW7_Q4.summary: A short street interview from Invisible People with Keith, a homeless man in Los Angeles who lost his housing-industry job in the crash and moved from painkillers to heroin because it was cheaper. He talks candidly about the grip of addiction.
H6ZFzEW7_Q4.why: HN commenters point to it in threads on homelessness and drug policy as a short, honest firsthand account from an articulate addict.

HMBl0ttu-Ow.summary: Sandy Pentland of MIT presents his book on social physics, which uses big-data studies of how people interact to explain how ideas spread. He describes findings on collective intelligence and social influence.
HMBl0ttu-Ow.why: HN commenters recommend it for the finding that idea exchange and connectivity drive productivity and wealth, which they apply to cities, offices and online communities.

HPqGaIMVuLs.summary: Rune Skovbo Johansen explains Surface-Stable Fractal Dithering, a technique he invented and released as open source. It makes dithering stick to 3D surfaces and covers the experiments and shortcomings along the way, inspired by Return of the Obra Dinn.
HPqGaIMVuLs.why: HN recommends it as the original explainer for a clever dithering technique and the go-to video in dithering threads.

HSxSgbNQi-g.summary: A short Wendover Productions explainer on ETOPS, the rules that let twin-engine jets fly long routes over oceans. It covers the economics that favored twinjets like the 787 over four-engine aircraft like the A380 and 747.
HSxSgbNQi-g.why: HN recommends it whenever threads touch twin-engine ocean flights, diversions, or why the 747 and A380 are being retired.

HfNIiitVFtc.summary: Patricia Aas's EuroBSDCon keynote is about ethics for people who build software, covering how the tech industry got to its current state and what engineers can do about it. It steps back from technical detail to the bigger picture.
HfNIiitVFtc.why: HN commenters strongly recommend it as a thoughtful talk on tech worker ethics that has not aged.

HlUe0TUHOIc.summary: Chris Domas's DEF CON 23 talk on psychological warfare against reverse engineers. He builds code whose disassembly and control flow graphs mislead, intimidate and demoralize anyone analyzing it.
HlUe0TUHOIc.why: Recommended as an entertaining and well-explained talk on anti-reverse-engineering tricks.

Hzb37RyagCQ.summary: A 36C3 talk by Bunnie Huang arguing that open source is necessary but not sufficient for trustworthy hardware, because verifying hardware is destructive and so creates a time-of-check/time-of-use gap. It surveys supply chain security and classes of hardware attacks, and presents the Betrusted approach to narrowing that gap.
Hzb37RyagCQ.why: HN commenters point to it whenever the question is how far hardware can be trusted, including FPGAs, supply chain attacks and firmware TPMs.

HM1Zb3xmvMc.summary: A playful music video promoting the book Land of Lisp, with a song about Lisp programming.
HM1Zb3xmvMc.why: HN shares it as a fun, cheerful introduction to Lisp culture that people say they rewatch.

HXAW2GseICs.summary: A short, nearly wordless demonstration of making sourdough pizza at home using a cast iron pan and the oven. It shows a Neapolitan-style result without a pizza steel or stone.
HXAW2GseICs.why: HN commenters recommend it as a practical, home-bakable sourdough pizza method that gets close to stone-oven quality.

Hd_ptbiPoXM.summary: Steve Jobs' 2005 Stanford commencement address, in which he tells three stories from his life about connecting the dots, love and loss, and death. He urges graduates to follow their dreams and find opportunity in setbacks.
Hd_ptbiPoXM.why: HN people point to it as an inspiring, rewatchable speech, especially for anyone worrying about wasted time or direction.

HhGI-GqAK9c.summary: Tom Murphy's satirical SIGBOVIK 2007 presentation, delivered under a pseudonym, proving that generalized Super Mario Bros. is NP-complete. It is a short, deadpan take on a complexity theory result.
HhGI-GqAK9c.why: HN likes it as a funny, entertaining presentation, frequently linked in threads on NP-hardness of games and NES automation.

HhGuXCuDb1U.summary: Animated adaptation of Tim Minchin's beat poem 'Storm', in which he argues with a hippie at a London dinner party. It satirizes alternative medicine and defends science and reason.
HhGuXCuDb1U.why: Quoted often for its line on alternative medicine that works being called medicine, and recommended as a full-length listen.

HrUy1Vn2KdI.summary: A 2017 documentary filmed at the Santa Fe Institute in which novelist Cormac McCarthy talks with SFI's David Krakauer. They discuss isolation, mathematics, character and the nature of the unconscious.
HrUy1Vn2KdI.why: It is one of the few long, candid interviews with the famously reclusive McCarthy, and commenters share it whenever he comes up.

H62hZJVqs2o.summary: A Strange Loop 2019 talk by Aaron Cummings on the computing systems aboard Voyager 1 and 2, which control the spacecraft and record and return data decades after launch in 1977.
H62hZJVqs2o.why: HN recommends it in Voyager threads as a good talk on how these old computers have proved durable and adaptable.

HBluLfX2F_k.summary: Veritasium explains why many real-world systems follow power laws rather than normal distributions. It covers self-organized criticality, with simulations of sandpiles, magnetism and forest fires.
HBluLfX2F_k.why: HN commenters recommend it for changing how they think about distributions and for showing how criticality shows up across earthquakes, wildfires and other fields.

HNkLcD3PKyk.summary: An Odd Lots podcast episode on why converting empty office buildings into apartments is hard. A managing director at Vanbarton Group walks through the zoning, financing and construction obstacles, mostly in New York.
HNkLcD3PKyk.why: HN links it whenever office-to-residential conversion comes up, as a good deep dive into why the idea is not simple.

HQKy1KJpSVc.summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day tours a Kodak factory to show how photographic film is manufactured. This is part one of a three-part series covering the large-scale coating and production process.
HQKy1KJpSVc.why: HN viewers find the film manufacturing process and the engineering behind it fascinating, especially the continuous roll changes.

HStF1RJOyxI.summary: Jan Vitek of Northeastern University gives a meetup talk on the challenges of making the R language run fast. He explains what in R's semantics makes it hard to optimize and to build a JIT compiler for.
HStF1RJOyxI.why: HN points to it as the best explanation of why R is so hard to optimize, often paired with talks on Python and used to explain what makes Julia fast.

HVv_IQKlafQ.summary: A two-minute explainer of 3D Gaussian Splatting, the rendering technique from a 2023 research paper. It outlines why it could change how 3D graphics are made.
HVv_IQKlafQ.why: HN uses it as a quick, non-expert primer whenever Gaussian splatting comes up.

HbUnatPfSgg.summary: Mike Arrington of TechCrunch speaks at Startup School 2008 about how to get press coverage for a startup and how to respond to it.
HbUnatPfSgg.why: HN recommends it as practical advice on dealing with tech press, whenever someone asks how to pitch TechCrunch and similar outlets.

H-XfCl-HpRM.summary: Andrew Huberman introduces how the nervous system produces sensation, emotion and behavior, and how neuroplasticity lets us change it. It covers neurons, synapses, brain chemicals and the rhythms governing focus, learning and sleep.
H-XfCl-HpRM.why: HN points to it as a foundational neuroscience primer, with some commenters crediting it for practical changes to learning and sleep.

H2tuKiiznsY.summary: Vox explainer arguing the two Boeing 737 Max crashes were not just a software bug but the result of a company's drive to beat its rival, with a flawed MCAS design.
H2tuKiiznsY.why: HN recommends it as a concise explanation of what caused the 737 Max crashes.

HMYiktO0D64.summary: A 1973 AT&T training film made for new employees at Bell Labs' Holmdel Computing Center, when Unix was in its third version and running at 16 computer centers in the Bell System. It shows how users submitted jobs and used the center's machines.
HMYiktO0D64.why: HN commenters share it as a rare, atmospheric look at what working at an early computing center was actually like, including how code was submitted and processed.

HNziOoXDBeg.summary: Kitboga baits tech-support scammers into believing they will get $3,000, wasting hours of their time while he plays along and screen-shares. The scammers become frustrated as it becomes clear the money will not reach them.
HNziOoXDBeg.why: HN commenters point to Kitboga as an entertaining, righteous example of wasting scammers' time.

HZGCoVF3YvM.summary: 3Blue1Brown presents Bayes' theorem through a geometric diagram, showing how evidence should update beliefs. It works through the Kahneman and Tversky style questions and base rates.
HZGCoVF3YvM.why: HN people recommend it as the most intuitive introduction to Bayes' theorem and cite it in base-rate arguments.

HlAXp0-M6SY.summary: Kelsey Hightower introduces Kubernetes to sysadmins at PuppetConf 2016, with a demo. He explains the declarative model and how it changes the contract between infrastructure and applications.
HlAXp0-M6SY.why: HN recommends it for Hightower's clear mental models, such as comparing the scheduler to Tetris and explaining why resource limits matter.

HrVtA-ue-x0.summary: Greg Wilson surveys what empirical research actually shows about software development, why we believe it, and how to share that knowledge more widely. It covers evidence on practices such as TDD and design patterns.
HrVtA-ue-x0.why: HN people recommend it as an evidence-based counterweight to opinion in software engineering debates.

H1KP4ztKK0A.summary: Dialect coach Erik Singer and several linguists tour distinct accents across English-speaking North America. It is the first part of a WIRED series on US accents.
H1KP4ztKK0A.why: HN recommends it as an enjoyable overview of American accents and what accent signals socially.

HA7GwKXfJB0.summary: Sebastian Seung's TED talk introduces the connectome, the map of neural connections he argues defines each person. He explains how mapping it could change how we understand brains and minds.
HA7GwKXfJB0.why: HN links it as an accessible visual explanation of the problem of mapping brain connectivity.

HE6rSljTwdU.summary: CaspianReport explainer arguing that Russia's geography, especially its vast size and indefensible Moscow core, shapes its political behavior. It frames Russian security thinking through the lens of geographic determinism.
HE6rSljTwdU.why: Offered as a concise summary of Russian security concerns and why Russia reacts as it does to NATO and Europe.

HF-9Dy6iB_4.summary: A PBS Space Time episode asking whether the universe's information can ever truly be lost, tying quantum mechanics, determinism and black holes together. It sets up the black hole information paradox.
HF-9Dy6iB_4.why: HN commenters point to it as an accessible explanation of abstract modern physics around the black hole information problem.

HF1luRD4Qmk.summary: Paul Irish's Chrome Dev Summit 2016 talk surveys the state of the art in Chrome DevTools debugging. It covers workspaces, diffs, CSS coverage, Node debugging, editor improvements and Lighthouse.
HF1luRD4Qmk.why: HN commenters cite it as a roundup of useful DevTools features and tips from Paul Irish.

HUMGc8hEkpc.summary: A PBS Space Time episode explaining why faster-than-light travel is equivalent to travelling back in time, using relativity and Minkowski diagrams for different observers.
HUMGc8hEkpc.why: HN points to it in warp drive discussions as a math-free explanation of why superluminal travel causes causality problems.

HfHgUu_8KgA.summary: Tom Scott explains why Britain historically has separate hot and cold taps rather than mixer taps, tracing it to how water was stored in tanks. He notes why the hot tap is not safe to drink from.
HfHgUu_8KgA.why: HN commenters treat it as the standard short answer whenever UK taps come up.

HipTO_7mUOw.summary: An 8-minute fictional short film, made by campaigners for a ban on autonomous weapons, depicting swarms of cheap AI-guided micro-drones used to kill targeted people. It ends with a call to action against autonomous weapons.
HipTO_7mUOw.why: HN cites it whenever drone swarms or autonomous weapons come up, as a dramatized warning that now feels increasingly plausible.

HmL2l-bcuUQ.summary: Kirsten Dirksen visits the Providence Arcade, the oldest US indoor mall, which was converted into 225-square-foot micro-lofts classified as a rooming house.
HmL2l-bcuUQ.why: Pointed to as a detailed example of converting a dying mall into housing.

HnOix9TFy1A.summary: Nadia Polikarpova's Strange Loop talk on program synthesis driven by refinement types, as in Synquid. It shows how rich type specifications can be turned into verified, executable code.
HnOix9TFy1A.why: HN points to it as a motivating introduction to what program synthesis is and what types can do for it.

Ho_CFfdsmc8.summary: Ben Vallack compares finger movement on a staggered keyboard with an ortholinear grid keyboard, using an Anne Pro 2 and a ZSA Planck EZ. He argues the stagger forces awkward finger motion.
Ho_CFfdsmc8.why: HN links it in keyboard threads as a short visual demonstration of why staggered layouts force unnatural finger movement.

HG6c4Kwbv4I.summary: Matt Godbolt builds a toy path tracer in C++ in three different styles and compares them on clarity, testability, compile time and run-time performance. The talk was given at CppCon 2019.
HG6c4Kwbv4I.why: HN points to it as a concrete demonstration of object-oriented versus cache-friendly design and the performance effects of branch misprediction.

HUngLgGRJpo.summary: "Nuggets" is a five-minute animated short by Andreas Hykade in which a kiwi bird tastes a golden nugget and keeps chasing the high. It works as a parable about addiction, habituation and withdrawal.
HUngLgGRJpo.why: HN commenters use it as a wordless illustration of addiction, shared in threads about children and screens, drugs and habit-forming products.

HgWHeT_OwHc.summary: The day one keynote of Google Cloud's 2016 GCP NEXT conference, with Sundar Pichai, Diane Greene, Eric Schmidt, Urs Holzle and customers. It includes a Cloud ML demo by Jeff Dean.
HgWHeT_OwHc.why: HN cites it as evidence of Google's cloud commitment and for Jeff Dean's talk-and-code demo.

HllUoT_WE7Y.summary: Peter Hutterer's linux.conf.au 2020 talk on creating libinput, the unified userspace input library, and the difficulties of handling the many quirks of input devices.
HllUoT_WE7Y.why: Cited for insight into the hard realities of Linux input handling and libinput's thinly staffed maintenance.

HxSHIpEQRjs.summary: Brandt Bucher presents his prototype JIT compiler for CPython at the 2023 Core Developer Sprint. He explains the copy-and-patch approach, the implementation and its performance.
HxSHIpEQRjs.why: It is the go-to explanation of how CPython's JIT works and why its design is so simple.

H7PJ1oeEyGg.summary: A four-minute Velocity 2011 talk in which Artur Bergman, then at Wikia, argues bluntly and with profanity that SSDs should replace spinning disks in servers.
H7PJ1oeEyGg.why: Cited as the memorable case for moving to SSDs and as an example of how swearing can make a talk stick.

HLAzeHnNgR8.summary: A short BBC HARDtalk clip from 2014 in which Senator John McCain says Putin aims to rebuild the Russian empire, starting with eastern Ukraine and then Moldova and the Baltics. He also criticizes Obama for not arming Ukraine.
HLAzeHnNgR8.why: Shared after 2022 as evidence that McCain accurately predicted Russian aggression and the cost of showing weakness.

HM23sjhtk4Q.summary: A clip from Tesla Autonomy Day 2019 where Elon Musk argues cameras are enough for self-driving and calls lidar a fool's errand.
HM23sjhtk4Q.why: Cited in self-driving threads as the source of Tesla's vision-only stance, usually to discuss or push back on it.

HNQ3GccCAI0.summary: A ten-minute explainer from Hypermind on the wisdom of crowds, covering Galton's discovery and the diversity theorem. It argues that collective intelligence comes from diversity, independence and aggregation.
HNQ3GccCAI0.why: HN people cite it as a short explanation of how aggregated individual guesses approach the truth.

HT_KdFCVEdc.summary: A short urbanism video presenting original observations of how drivers treat stop signs, to argue that cyclists rolling through them under an Idaho stop is no different. It filmed intersections in Ottawa.
HT_KdFCVEdc.why: Linked in threads on the Idaho and Colorado safety stop as evidence that drivers already roll stop signs.

HTzw_grLzjw.summary: A FoundMyFitness episode on how microplastics and associated chemicals such as BPA and PFAS accumulate in the body, including the brain and reproductive systems. It also discusses ways to reduce exposure.
HTzw_grLzjw.why: Mentioned occasionally as an episode on environmental toxins in food and water, though one commenter lumps it in with unregulated quackery.

HUti6vGctQM.summary: A four-minute minutephysics video arguing that causal models and causal networks let statistics infer causation from correlation. It touches on Reichenbach's principle, common causes, feedback and quantum causal discovery.
HUti6vGctQM.why: HN people link it as a short, accessible summary of Judea Pearl-style causal inference when someone repeats that correlation cannot imply causation.

Hatav_Rdnno.summary: Engineering Explained argues that internal combustion engines are far from dead, and discusses the continued development of ICEs and the problems facing electric vehicles.
Hatav_Rdnno.why: Cited as a balanced engineering view of improvements in both ICE and EV technology.

Hdpf-MQM9vY.summary: Time-lapse of Broad Group erecting a 30-story prefabricated hotel (J57) in Changsha, China in about 15 days. The description touts modular construction's precision, speed and low waste.
Hdpf-MQM9vY.why: Shared as a striking example of what prefab modular construction can achieve in speed.

HgtRAbE1nBM.summary: Bryan Cantrill's QCon SF 2019 talk asking whether operating systems should be rewritten in Rust. He draws on his systems experience to discuss C, memory safety and Rust's fit for system software.
HgtRAbE1nBM.why: Cited in debates about Rust versus C as a thoughtful systems programmer's account of falling for Rust.

HjHMoNGqQTI.summary: The Hated One argues that Kurzgesagt acts as a propaganda vehicle for its billionaire-linked sponsors, citing funding it received. The video prompted a response from Kurzgesagt.
HjHMoNGqQTI.why: Mostly used as a critical source on how popular science channels may be shaped by billionaire funding.

HkZDSqyE1do.summary: A short documentary about Jadav Payeng, who since the 1970s has planted a forest larger than Central Park on India's Majuli island, turning barren land into a lush oasis.
HkZDSqyE1do.why: HN commenters share it as an inspiring example of one person restoring an ecosystem by planting trees.

Hl1zEzVUV7w.summary: Tesla's 2023 Investor Day, a nearly four-hour presentation covering Master Plan 3, vehicle design, powertrain, electronic architecture, manufacturing and sustainable energy economics.
Hl1zEzVUV7w.why: HN commenters cite it as a primary source for Tesla's claims on battery materials, assembly design, 48V architecture and energy investment.

HlmKejRSVd8.summary: Isaac Arthur examines Dyson spheres and swarms, including common myths and misconceptions. He covers uses such as interstellar travel, black hole generation, and computing large enough to simulate universes.
HlmKejRSVd8.why: HN references it in threads on megastructures, Kardashev civilizations and Dyson sphere detection, and recommends the channel for in-depth futurist content.

H-gfxjAaZg0.summary: A comedy song by Garfunkel and Oates in which both play the same woman at 29 and at 31, charting a swift slide in her romantic prospects.
H-gfxjAaZg0.why: Cited in threads on dating, loneliness and the shortage of eligible partners as a song that captures the dilemma.

H110vCGvTmM.summary: An undercover report from the 2019 Flat Earth Conference by the comedy channel All Gas No Brakes, which interviews attendees on camera.
H110vCGvTmM.why: HN mentions it mostly as an amusing look at flat earthers in their own words, not as a recommendation.

H27rfr59RiE.summary: A one-minute clip from The Simpsons in which Homer is bought out by Bill Gates. It is a short cartoon scene that parodies Gates and Microsoft.
H27rfr59RiE.why: HN mostly uses it as a joke or a reference point when discussing buyouts, Gates's competitiveness, or Microsoft's public image in the 1990s.

H4ThZcq1oJQ.summary: CBS News clip from a 2016 Republican primary debate in which Donald Trump attacks George W. Bush over 9/11 and the Iraq War while Jeb Bush defends his brother. It is a short, heated exchange on national security records.
H4ThZcq1oJQ.why: Cited as the moment Trump supposedly broke the Bush dynasty's hold on the GOP by making the Iraq War a wedge issue.

H6F0PgMcKWM.summary: Matt Mullenweg joins ThePrimeagen's Twitch stream to discuss the WordPress and WP Engine dispute, including trademark use and contributions.
H6F0PgMcKWM.why: HN cites it as the primary source for Mullenweg's own statements during the WP Engine dispute, though some found him unprepared.

H7Uyfqi_TE8.summary: Elon Musk's 2016 IAC presentation on the technical challenges and architectures for building a self-sustaining human presence on Mars.
H7Uyfqi_TE8.why: Referenced as Musk's original statement of SpaceX's multiplanetary plan.

H8eP99neOVs.summary: A three-minute clip of Steve Jobs at WWDC 1997 explaining that focus means saying no to many good ideas. It is a short answer about product strategy and its effect on people.
H8eP99neOVs.why: HN uses it as the canonical source for the 'focus is saying no' quote, cited in threads on product decisions such as dropping old hardware support.

HAZP-RNSr0s.summary: A short local news report about a Waymo self-driving car that crashed into a pole in downtown Phoenix.
HAZP-RNSr0s.why: HN cites it as evidence that robotaxis can still have odd, avoidable crashes, usually in threads that criticize self-driving safety claims.

HGYFEI6uLy0.summary: Apple's 1987 Knowledge Navigator concept video imagines a conversational voice assistant, multi-touch tablet and video calling used by a professor. It was made years before the graphical web existed.
HGYFEI6uLy0.why: HN cites it as an early vision of voice assistants and software agents, often when comparing it with Siri and modern AI.

HHjgK6p4nrw.summary: Guy Kawasaki's UC Berkeley Haas talk on the top ten mistakes entrepreneurs make, covering a startup from inception to exit.
HHjgK6p4nrw.why: HN uses it as a reference for startup advice such as not befriending your VC, linear thinking in valuations, and protecting ideas.

HKTSaezB4p8.summary: A one-minute clip of Richard Feynman playing bongos with his best friend.
